We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(e,1).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{x} \\ {f}^{′}(e) & =\frac{1}{e}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(e,1)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(1,e)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(1))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(e)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{e})} \\  & =e.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
